title: Author safely alongside concurrent writers
statement: As a developer collaborating in parallel, I can submit a Saga mutation without overwriting another writer's newer work so concurrent edits remain recoverable.
overview:
Independent authors can add separate records, but a mutation to an existing history must name the parent it actually read. Cooperative locks serialize writes; a busy writer can retry, while a stale parent requires rereading and deciding how to incorporate concurrent work.

The storage layer stages file and directory publication and attempts rollback for a failed batch. This is not a global multi-file crash transaction. [Storage and evolution](/technical/pages/storage) explains the failure boundary and why direct metadata edits bypass the intended checks.

acceptance_criteria.statement: When two supported writers overlap, one completes its persisted mutation before the other changes Saga state; a writer that cannot proceed within the configured timeout returns a busy error.
A revision whose submitted parent set differs from the current head set is rejected without creating the revision and identifies the expected heads.
